images.title: One cube on isometric paper
images.purpose: Pictures the simplest state of the isometric grid builder: one unit cube on the grid with its three drawing directions.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. A faint isometric grid fills the frame; one cube sits in the centre with three arrows from one corner.
images.exact_structure: Background: a faint grey isometric grid of vertical lines and two families of lines slanting at 30 degrees above horizontal, left and right. One unit cube drawn on it, each edge 1 grid unit: top rhombus filled light teal #0072B2, left face medium teal, right face darker teal, 9 visible edges outlined dark. From a grid point 1 unit below and in front of the cube's nearest bottom corner (clear of the cube), three bold reddish purple #CC79A7 arrows along the grid, each 2 units long: straight up labelled 'height', up to the right labelled 'length', up to the left labelled 'depth'. The cube's front top edge running up to the right is marked with a small bracket above it labelled '1 unit'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: On isometric paper vertical lines are height and the two slants are length and depth, with equal units on each.
images.description: Pictures the simplest state of the isometric grid builder: one unit cube on the grid with its three drawing directions.
images.context: Concept T13.C4; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Teal shades on the cube count as one accent; the arrows share one colour so the labels name them.

image_decisions.why: A practice concept for the isometric grid builder; the image fixes its three directions in the simplest case.
